## Three steps

[`deva2iast`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ganapati/metre.html#deva2iast)
writes the text in Latin letters keeping vowel length.
[`syllables`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ganapati/metre.html#syllables)
marks each syllable heavy or light and
[`scan`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ganapati/metre.html#scan) returns
that as a `g`/`l` string.
[`detect_meter`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ganapati/metre.html#detect_meter)
matches it against the tables. A syllable is heavy when its vowel is
long or a consonant cluster follows.

`fold_token` throws vowel length away so a search matches either
spelling. Metre needs length, so
[`deva2iast`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ganapati/metre.html#deva2iast)
is a second transliteration rather than a reuse of the fold.

### deva2iast

``` python
def deva2iast(
    s:str
)->str:
```

*Devanagari to IAST, keeping the vowel length that scansion depends on.*

``` python
from ganapati.metre import deva2iast
```

``` python
assert deva2iast('श्रीमाता') == 'śrīmātā'
assert deva2iast('देवी') == 'devī'
assert deva2iast('कर्म') == 'karma'      # the virāma kills the implicit vowel
assert deva2iast('गम्') == 'gam'
assert deva2iast('दे॒वी') == 'devī'      # the Vedic tone mark is stripped first
```

`ai` and `au` are one vowel each, `kh` and `th` one consonant each, so
`atha` is two syllables. A consonant closing one syllable does not open
the next: in `kaṃsa` the `ṃ` belongs to `kaṃ`.

### syllables

``` python
def syllables(
    text:str
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
```

*The syllables of a Sanskrit string as `(syllable, guru)` pairs.*

``` python
import unicodedata
from ganapati.metre import syllables, scan
```

``` python
assert [s for s, _ in syllables('atha')] == ['a', 'tha']      # `th` is one consonant
assert [s for s, _ in syllables('kaṃsa')] == ['kaṃ', 'sa']    # the ṃ closes the first, not opens the second
assert scan('gam') == 'g'                                     # a final cluster makes it heavy
assert scan('rāma') == 'gl'                                   # long ā, then a bare short a
assert scan('īśā vāsyam idaṃ sarvaṃ') == 'gggllggg'
assert scan(unicodedata.normalize('NFD', 'īśā vāsyam idaṃ sarvaṃ')) == 'gggllggg'   # decomposed IAST keeps its long vowels
```

## The gaṇas

A gaṇa is a named triple of weights. Eight cover every triple; `ga` and
`la` fill a leftover one or two. `METERS` stores each metre as a recipe
of gaṇa names, the way the tradition states them, and
[`ganas`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ganapati/metre.html#ganas) reads
a pattern back into names. That is what `by_meter` searches on.

The āryā family counts morae instead: a light syllable is one, a heavy
two, built from four-mora gaṇas with one position that shrinks.
[`detect_matra_meter`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ganapati/metre.html#detect_matra_meter)
fits weights into slots rather than matching a fixed string.

### detect_ardhasama

``` python
def detect_ardhasama(
    text:str, weights:list=None
):
```

*The ardhasamavṛtta of a verse — `AttrDict(name, padas, ganas)` — or
None.*

``` python
# Meghadūta 1.1, four pādas of seventeen syllables
mand = ('kaścit kāntāvirahaguruṇā svādhikārātpramattaḥ '
        'śāpenāstaṃgamitamahimā varṣabhogyeṇa bhartuḥ '
        'yakṣaścakre janakatanayāsnānapuṇyodakeṣu '
        'snigdhacchāyātaruṣu vasatiṃ rāmagiryāśrameṣu')
m = detect_meter(mand)
assert m.name is Meter.MANDAKRANTA and m.per_pada == 17
assert m.ganas == 'ma bha na ta ta ga ga'

# Gītā 1.1: the anuṣṭubh, and which of its variants
a = detect_meter('dharmakṣetre kurukṣetre samavetā yuyutsavaḥ '
                 'māmakāḥ pāṇḍavāścaiva kimakurvata sañjaya')
assert a.name is Meter.ANUSTUBH and a.variant == 'pathyā' and a.per_pada == 8

assert Meter.VASANTATILAKA.value == 'vasantatilakā'
assert Meter.MANDAKRANTA == 'mandākrāntā'
```

## Partial verses

Forced alignment, ASR and line-per-record TEI hand you one line at a
time, with no daṇḍa left to split on.
[`detect_meter`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ganapati/metre.html#detect_meter)
needs a whole verse, so both of these work below it.
[`match_pada`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ganapati/metre.html#match_pada)
names the metres a single pāda fits.
[`group_verses`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ganapati/metre.html#group_verses)
tries 1, 2 and 4 lines per verse and keeps the grouping that names the
most metres: 4 for the Meghadūta, 2 for a Rāmāyaṇa aligned half-verse at
a time.

### match_pada

``` python
def match_pada(
    pada:str
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
```

*The metres one pāda could belong to — what
[`detect_meter`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ganapati/metre.html#detect_meter)
cannot say from a partial verse.*

``` python
# one pāda of the Meghadūta, which detect_meter can only call unmatched
padas = ['kaścit kāntāvirahaguruṇā svādhikārātpramattaḥ',
         'śāpenāstaṃgamitamahimā varṣabhogyeṇa bhartuḥ',
         'yakṣaścakre janakatanayāsnānapuṇyodakeṣu',
         'snigdhacchāyātaruṣu vasatiṃ rāmagiryāśrameṣu']
assert detect_meter(padas[0]).name is None              # an AttrDict, never None
assert Meter.MANDAKRANTA in match_pada(padas[0])
assert match_pada('gglggllglgg') == [Meter.INDRAVAJRA]  # a g/l pattern reads the same way

# the four lines with no daṇḍa anywhere: the grouping has to be guessed
g = group_verses(padas)
assert g.size == 4 and g.coverage == 1.0
assert g.meters[0].name is Meter.MANDAKRANTA
assert group_verses([]).coverage == 0.0
```

``` python
# Kumārasambhava 4.1, viyoginī: the odd pādas are 10 syllables, the even 11
K41 = ('अथ मोहपरायणा सती विवशा कामवधूर्विबोधिता ।\n'
       'विधिना प्रतिपादयिष्यता नववैधव्यमसह्यवेदनम् ॥')
m = detect_meter(K41)
assert m.name == Meter.VIYOGINI and m.syllables == 42 and m.per_pada is None

# and its closing verse, puṣpitāgrā: 12 + 13
K446 = ('अथ मदनवधूरुपप्लवान्तं व्यसनकृशा परिपालयां बभूव ।\n'
        'शशिन इव दिवातनस्य लेखा किरणपरिक्षयधूसरा प्रदोषम् ॥')
assert detect_meter(K446).name == Meter.PUSPITAGRA

# a samavṛtta is still named by the pāda table, not relabelled by the new one
assert detect_meter(' '.join(padas)).name == Meter.MANDAKRANTA
```

## Duration against scansion

An aligned source is the one place a scansion can be checked against
something outside itself.
[`line_times`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ganapati/text.html#line_times)
gives each line’s milliseconds,
[`matras`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ganapati/metre.html#matras)
gives its morae, and the two should stay in proportion across a
recitation. A line that is far off the chunk’s median is either
mis-scanned or mis-aligned.
[`guru_laghu_ratio`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ganapati/metre.html#guru_laghu_ratio)
fits the two durations over many lines; the śāstra says 2:1, and
measurement over aligned Vedic recitation lands between 1.3 and 2.7.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/ganapati/blob/main/ganapati/metre.py#L377"

### mora_rate

``` python
def mora_rate(
    text:str
)->float:
```

*Milliseconds per mora over a chunk’s timed lines, or None when the
chunk carries no timings.*

``` python
from ganapati.text import time_marker
```

``` python
def timed(ps, rate=100):
    'Each pāda with an audio span that honours its morae at `rate` ms per mora.'
    rs = rate if isinstance(rate, list) else [rate] * len(ps)
    out, t = [], 0
    for p, r in zip(ps, rs):
        d = matras(p) * r; out.append(f'{p} {time_marker(t, t + d)}'); t += d
    return '\n'.join(out)

assert mora_rate(timed(padas)) == 100
assert timing_check(timed(padas)) == []
assert 1.99 < guru_laghu_ratio(timed(padas)) < 2.01     # a guru is two laghus, measured
assert timing_check(timed(padas, [100, 100, 100, 180]))[0].start == 8000  # the line out of proportion
assert mora_rate('\n'.join(padas)) is None              # no timings, nothing to measure
```
